## Page 12

Governance Plan
12
TISCO Financial Group | Investor RelationsAnti-Corruption 
“To strengthen integrity, transparency, and a 
zero-tolerance approach to corruption across 
TISCO and its supply chain.”
Anti-Corruption Policy, formally approved 
by the Board of Directors, includes clearly 
defined practices and guidelines, and is in 
place to encompass all business activities. 
The BOD provides annual review for anti -
corruption matters and updates the policy at 
least once a year.
Key direct suppliers (Critical Tier 1) are required 
to establish their own Anti -Corruption Policy 
which will be included in the supplier 
performance evaluation criteria. Board Independence
“To ensure adequate independence that 
enables balance power between the BOD and 
the management.”
In compliance with SEC CG Code, the 
Board of Directors requires to have 
independent directors at least one -third of 
total members.
Currently, t he Board of Directors comprises 
of 46% independent directors.
To align with OECD Principles of CG and SEC 
CG Code, the Board of Directors requires to 
comprise of independent directors exceeding 
50% of total board seats.AI Governance 
“To establish a responsible, transparent, and 
compliant AI governance framework within the 
organization.”
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy and 
Practi ces areestablished under the 
supervision of the BOD, and AI Governance 
is trained and communicated to all 
employees.
The responsible use of AI is audited and 
reported to the BOD, according to Responsible 
AI Reporting Framework Existing
